model_vs_rules.verdict: Model advantage over the order-value rule is not statistically established at any tested treated share (paired cluster-bootstrap CI includes 0).

checks.detail: 0% of cases have an explicit category SLA; 100% use the 240h fallback
120 of 9228 cases dropped from SLA labels

claims.claim: The model beats a simple order-value rule
claims.evidence: PO-isolated holdout, cluster bootstrap: paired CIs include 0 at 5-30% treated share (docs/model-vs-rules.md).

claims.claim: A look-ahead leak inflated supplier-history features
claims.evidence: History now uses only cases completed before the scored case starts; model retrained 2026-10-03.
Effects are assumptions; no real intervention outcomes recorded (docs/uplift-method.md).
Planted-anomaly evaluation: C1 97.5%, C4 80%, C3 66.7% recall (synthetic injections only).
Default SLA target is ~97% breach; realistic p75 targets give 0.78-0.93.
Anomaly flags only; no ground-truth fraud labels exist in any dataset used.

experiments.name: Isolation Forest vs rules (AP)
experiments.note: Did not beat the rule-based controls.

experiments.name: Supplier workload features
experiments.note: Did not beat rules at 5-10% treated.

experiments.name: Isotonic vs Platt calibration
experiments.note: Held-out Platt kept; isotonic fitted on train rows had collapsed AUC.

experiments.name: Duplicate invoice control on Online Retail II
experiments.note: 21x lift over base reversal rate (proxy label).

limitations: The event log is a closed historical replay: no live cases, so 'at risk' means the model's score on finished cases.
Supplier and user ids are anonymised; there are no bank accounts or devices to link.
Order value is the maximum net worth seen in the case, not an invoiced amount.
Most cases use the fallback SLA target rather than an explicit one.
Held-out cases cluster by purchase order, so confidence intervals remain optimistic.
